walkthroughs.body_html:
Cross Bb × Bb.

Write parent gametes B, b across and B, b down. Fill four boxes: BB, Bb, Bb, bb.

Genotype ratio 1:2:1. Phenotype ratio (B dominant) = 3:1.

From Bb × Bb the chance of a recessive phenotype (bb) is 1 in 4, or 25%.

The chance of being a carrier (Bb) is 2 in 4, or 50%. Quote ratio AND percentage for full marks.

Cystic fibrosis is recessive — allele f. Two carriers (Ff × Ff) have children.

Punnett gives FF: Ff: Ff: ff. So 1 in 4 (25%) have CF; 2 in 4 (50%) are unaffected carriers; 1 in 4 are unaffected non-carriers.

What does it mean for an allele to be 'dominant'?
options: Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.
A dominant allele is the most common allele in a population.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
It is expressed in the phenotype when at least one copy is present (in a heterozygote).

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
No — humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor; both have evolved from it.
Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
Humans evolved directly from chimpanzees, which is why chimps still exist as a less-evolved version.
